az_crown_butte.blurb: Crown Butte is the standout summit between the Church Spires and Gibraltar Rock on the Sedona side of Highway 179. Most of the climbing is trad, with the longer multipitch lines on the west face and shorter cragging on the Backside Crag. The nine routes in this area are mostly in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, with a single easier line and one in the 5.11s. Expect a committed day: the trail climbs to the saddle shared with Gibraltar Rock, and the whole walk takes close to an hour. It is a quieter alternative to Sedona's busier roadside spires.
az_crown_butte.parking_note: Use the Little Horse Trailhead, which is south of the chapel along Highway 179.

_expect.name: An Undercling Thing / Burger King Boulder

az_an_undercling_thing_burger_king_bould.blurb: Two big boulders stand side by side, split by a narrow corridor, at the eastern end of the main Gloria's section above Flagstaff. There are nine problems, most between V0 and V5 with one much harder line near V7, so beginners and intermediates both have plenty to try. Taller slab problems on the next boulder along are also worth a look. The rock is dacite, which is rough on skin, and the setting is cool ponderosa forest where it is easy to follow the shade in summer. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons, and the boulders sit just a short walk from the Heart Cave.

az_anorexic_roof.blurb: This roof sits deep in Priest Draw, the limestone bouldering gully near Flagstaff, well beyond the closer walls that are a minute from parking. The nine problems here are powerful and steep, mostly in the V6 to V9 range with a couple of harder lines, so it is a destination for strong boulderers rather than people warming up. Plan on a real walk from the parking area to reach it, so bring enough pads and food for a full session.

az_perfect_day_wall.blurb: Perfect Day Wall is a small bouldering wall just west of the main Drysdale Trail on The Ridge, near Lake Mary outside Flagstaff. It is shorter than the neighboring walls, with nine problems from V0 to about V3, which makes it a friendly place to warm up or to climb with newer boulderers. A row of pockets runs along the right side, while the left side has chunky sloping holds. The hillside landing has been built up to give pads a flat spot. It sits roughly five minutes beyond the Gateway Wall.
az_perfect_day_wall.parking_note: Park off the dirt road north of the highway, just past the Lower Lake Mary Picnic Area entrance. Low-clearance cars should stop before the gate; otherwise use the pull-outs up the road past it.

_expect.name: South-Facing Wall (AKA the North Wall), The

az_south_facing_wall_aka_the_north_wall_.blurb: A newer wall in Lime Kiln Canyon, on the Arizona Strip east of Mesquite, close to the Grail Wall. It has nine routes, all sport, with the weight in the 5.11s: five routes land there, backed by a few 5.10s and a pair of easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. That makes it a spot for climbers who already lead low-to-mid 5.11. The cliff is described as loose in places, so helmets and care with falling rock are sensible. The canyon around it is a limestone sport venue best enjoyed in fall and spring.

az_sleeping_cactus_wall.blurb: One of three crags at the north end of Little Granite Mountain, on its east side in the McDowell Sonoran country north of Phoenix. It has nine routes, six traditional and three bolted, running from about 5.7 to 5.10, so it works well for newer leaders looking for moderate lines on desert granite. The rock quality is uneven in spots but generally fine. The wall gets morning sun and falls into shade around early afternoon, and it appears to be little visited. The last stretch of the approach is steep, brushy and rocky, and a rappel station with chains sits near the middle of the wall.
az_sleeping_cactus_wall.parking_note: Start from the Granite Mountain Trailhead, reached by driving north on 136th Street from Dynamite Road and turning left a short way west near the two-mile mark.
